name: Puerto Viejo Town
tagline: The main strip, reggae bars and the bike rental shops
description: The village itself, a few streets between the road and the sea with the bars, restaurants, supermarkets and bicycle rentals that make the place function. It is where the nightlife is, where most of the coworking happens, and where you can live without a vehicle.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bars, the cafes and the bike shops on the doorstep
pros: The bars, live music and the social scene
Best connectivity and the coworking spaces
cons: Loud on the strip at night
Theft from accommodation is a known problem

name: Playa Cocles
tagline: Two kilometres south, the surf beach and quieter cabinas
description: The long beach immediately south of town, with the area's most consistent surf, a scattering of cabinas and small restaurants set back under the trees, and a bike path running into the village. It is calmer than the strip while keeping it within five minutes by bicycle.
bestFor: Stays that want the surf beach and the town a short ride away
pros: The area's best surf directly there
Quieter than town but connected by the bike path
cons: Rip currents make it unsuitable for casual swimming

name: Punta Uva
tagline: The calmest water on the coast, seven kilometres south
description: A pair of sheltered coves either side of a rocky point, where the reef makes the water calm and clear enough to swim and snorkel properly, backed by rainforest with sloths and howler monkeys in the trees. Accommodation is scattered houses and small lodges.
bestFor: Stays that want swimmable water and rainforest rather than a village
pros: The calmest, clearest water on this coast
Rainforest and wildlife at the door
cons: A bicycle or car is essential
Twenty minutes by bike into town
Very few shops and slower internet

name: Manzanillo
tagline: The end of the road, at the edge of the wildlife refuge
description: The last village on the coast road, thirteen kilometres south, where the Gandoca-Manzanillo refuge begins and the coastal trail runs on through rainforest to empty beaches. It is a small Afro-Caribbean fishing village with a few sodas and cabinas and nothing else at all.
bestFor: Stays where the wildlife refuge matters more than any amenity
pros: The refuge and its coastal trail from the village
The emptiest beaches on this coast
cons: Almost no services and unreliable internet

name: Playa Negra and Cahuita Road
tagline: North of the village, black sand and lower rents
description: The black-sand beach immediately north of town and the road running on towards Cahuita, with houses and cabinas set among the trees at rents noticeably below the southern beaches. It is a five-minute walk or ride into the village and considerably quieter.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lower rents within walking distance of town
pros: Five minutes on foot or by bike into the village
cons: Black sand gets very hot and is less appealing
The road to Cahuita carries steady traffic
